reasons: One large file handles many separate jobs.
Only part of the file was reviewed, so the rating is partial.
Link addresses in the PDF export are not fully escaped.
The archive action deletes permanently while its label says archive.

terms.meaning: values the screen remembers while it is open, such as typed text or the current result
a new browser window opened by the app
earlier versions of AI text kept so the user can go back
suggestions for adding new facts to the profile, drawn from the user's notes

sections.name: File setup, STATUSES
sections.title: Imports and status list
sections.what: Imports the screen parts, storage helpers, AI helpers, and integration settings. Lists the allowed statuses in order.
sections.why: The status list drives the status buttons and their order.
sections.watch_out: Each status also needs a matching color style, or its button will look wrong.

sections.name: ApplicationDetail (part 1)
sections.title: Screen state and loading the application
sections.what: Sets up the screen's memory, such as the note being edited, AI output, errors, and version history. Loads the application when the slug changes.
sections.why: Each feature keeps its own state so one panel does not disturb another.
sections.watch_out: The record is read once per slug change, so edits made in another tab do not show until the page reloads.

sections.name: ApplicationDetail: if
sections.title: Not-found screen and status handlers
sections.what: Shows a not-found screen listing saved slugs when the record is missing. Defines handlers that change status, save notes, and save the next action.
sections.why: Setting status to applied also schedules a follow-up reminder.
sections.watch_out: Status changes save straight to storage with no confirmation.

sections.name: ApplicationDetail: if
sections.title: Dispatching document generation
sections.what: Checks that a profile exists, then calls the AI helper for the chosen document. Saves resume output. For the problem solver, first asks a research service for company context. Outreach types also queue a message for follow-up.
sections.why: Likely reason: each document type needs different inputs, so one dispatcher picks the right one.
sections.watch_out: If the research call fails, the error is silently ignored and the pitch is written without company context. The user may not notice.

sections.name: ApplicationDetail (part 4)
sections.title: Copy, refine, and undo
sections.what: Copies AI output to the clipboard, sends a refinement instruction to the AI, saves the previous version, and can revert to it.
sections.why: Lets the user edit AI text in small steps without losing earlier versions.
sections.watch_out: Version history exists only in screen memory, so a page reload clears it.

sections.name: ApplicationDetail (part 5)
sections.title: Profile suggestions and Markdown download
sections.what: Sends notes of at least 40 characters to a service that suggests profile additions. Downloads AI output as a Markdown file. Also starts the helper that converts Markdown into HTML for the PDF.
sections.why: Likely reason: notes often reveal achievements missing from the profile, and a Markdown file is an easy download.
sections.watch_out: Short notes never produce suggestions, because of the 40-character minimum.

sections.name: ApplicationDetail: for
sections.title: Markdown to print page
sections.what: Turns the AI output into HTML one line at a time, then writes it into a new window with print styling and a Save as PDF button.
sections.why: Likely reason: writing a print page avoids adding a PDF library. The code does not state this.
sections.watch_out: Link addresses are placed into HTML attributes after only basic escaping, so a quote mark in a link could break the page.

sections.name: window load handler (part 1)
sections.title: Print scaling, archive, and update parsing
sections.what: Inside the new window, a script shrinks the text if the page would run past one page. Also holds the archive action, which asks for confirmation, and the request that sends typed updates to the parsing route.
sections.why: Likely reason: the scaling keeps long resumes on one page, and archive asks first because deletion is permanent.
sections.watch_out: Archive permanently deletes the record even though the button says archive.

sections.name: window load handler: if
sections.title: Applying a confirmed update and page start
sections.what: Turns a confirmed parse into one set of changes: status, a dated note, a new interview, and a contact. Saves them and shows a confirmation. Also starts the page layout with a link back to the pipeline.
sections.why: Likely reason: one combined save keeps the record consistent.
sections.watch_out: Reminders are only scheduled in two narrow cases, so a status change to something other than applied with a reminder day schedules nothing.

sections.name: window load handler (part 3)
sections.title: Title block and update box
sections.what: Shows the company, role, location, status, age, and bucket, with status buttons. Also shows the box where the user types a plain-language update.
sections.why: Puts the key facts and quick actions at the top of the screen.
sections.watch_out: The status buttons save immediately with no undo.

sections.name: window load handler (part 4)
sections.title: Review panel for parsed updates
sections.what: Shows what the AI understood from the update, such as status, interview, contact, reminder, and note, so the user can confirm or dismiss it.
sections.why: Likely reason: AI parsing can be wrong, so the user confirms before anything is saved.
sections.watch_out: Dates appear as the AI wrote them, so a wrong date is only noticed here.

sections.name: window load handler (part 5)
sections.title: Score card in left column
sections.what: Starts the left column of the application page with the score card. It shows an A-F evaluation with an overall number, the archetype label, and five scores (CV match, north star, comp, culture, red flags), each with its reasoning. If no full evaluation exists, it shows a simple match score with a bar instead.
sections.why: Likely reason: the score is the first thing a reader needs when deciding whether to pursue the job.
sections.watch_out: The number colours use fixed cut-offs at 4.5, 4.0 and 3.5, so changing the scale also changes which numbers look good.

sections.name: window load handler (part 6)
sections.title: Match score bar and next action buttons
sections.what: Finishes the simple match score, showing the number and a bar of filled and empty blocks with the bucket name. Then it opens the next action box, which shows the saved next step and offers quick buttons. The buttons that appear depend on words in that step, such as tailor, apply, outreach, skip or review.
sections.why: Likely reason: the buttons are chosen from the next step text so the user sees only the actions that seem relevant.
sections.watch_out: Button choice uses simple word matching, so editing the next step text can add or remove buttons unexpectedly.

sections.name: window load handler (part 7)
sections.title: Mark done, action panel and error links
sections.what: Ends the next action box with a MARK DONE button that clears the next step and saves that change. Then shows the main action panel with buttons to tailor a resume, write a cover letter, create an executive summary, make a problem solver pitch, run a skill gap analysis, draft outreach and LinkedIn messages, write a CEO cold email, find contacts, and archive. All generation buttons are disabled while any generation runs. If an error mentions Settings or the profile, it also shows a link to fix that.
sections.why: Likely reason: all document generation sits in one place, with a shortcut to fix missing setup.
sections.watch_out: The archive buttons call the same handler with no confirmation prompt visible in this section.

sections.name: window load handler (part 8)
sections.title: Contacts panel and generated output
sections.what: Shows the contacts panel when the user clicks find contacts and a profile exists. Then shows the panel for the latest AI result, with a heading that matches the document type and buttons to copy, download as Markdown, export to PDF, or close. If the AI returns nothing, it shows a warning and a regenerate button.
sections.why: Likely reason: the empty response warning exists because AI providers sometimes return nothing, for example when rate limited.
sections.watch_out: The heading only covers known document types, so a new type would appear with no title.

sections.name: window load handler (part 9)
sections.title: Refine box to edit generated text
sections.what: Lets the user type a change request for the generated text, such as removing a line or rewriting a paragraph. It shows how many edits have been made and an UNDO LAST button. The user can click apply or press Cmd or Ctrl plus Enter. The box is disabled while the AI is working.
sections.why: Likely reason: users can fix output without rewriting it by hand, and undo gives a way back if an edit goes wrong.
sections.watch_out: Undo relies on the saved version history, so the edit count and undo must stay in step with every change.

sections.name: window load handler (part 10)
sections.title: Saved resume with copy and edit
sections.what: Shows the resume stored on the application, with buttons to copy it, edit it, and export it as a PDF. Saving writes the edited text back to the stored application record and shows a brief SAVED label. Cancel drops unsaved edits.
sections.why: Likely reason: the final resume stays editable after generation, so small fixes can be made by hand.
sections.watch_out: Export PDF uses the edit box text while editing, so an exported PDF can differ from what is saved.

sections.name: window load handler (part 11)
sections.title: Notes box and skill gap readiness bar
sections.what: Shows the application notes with an edit toggle and a save button. When a skill gap analysis exists, shows a panel with a close button, a role readiness percentage with a bar, and a one-line summary. The bar is green at 75 percent or more, amber at 50 or more, and red below that.
sections.why: Likely reason: the colours give a quick read of fit without the user having to interpret the number.
sections.watch_out: If the readiness number is missing, the screen shows a bare percent sign with no value.

sections.name: window load handler (part 12)
sections.title: Strong, partial and missing skill lists
sections.what: Lists the skill gap results in three groups: strong matches with evidence, partial matches with the gap and a suggested fix, and missing skills with a priority label. Each group is hidden when it is empty.
sections.why: Likely reason: sorts the results into what already helps, what is close, and what to work on.
sections.watch_out: This section reads the length of each list directly, so if the AI output is missing one of these lists the page can crash.

sections.name: window load handler (part 13)
sections.title: Job description insights and keywords
sections.what: Shows AI-extracted details from the job description when they exist. This includes a years-required badge, a keyword cloud where each word can be clicked to copy and a button copies them all, and lists of technical and soft skills.
sections.why: Likely reason: the keywords help the user reuse the exact job wording in a resume, since applicant tracking software scans for it.
sections.watch_out: The keyword section is hidden when its list is empty, so a failed extraction looks the same as a job with no keywords.

sections.name: window load handler (part 14)
sections.title: Requirements, red flags, interviews and form answers
sections.what: Shows the key requirements as a bullet list and any red flags in a red box. Then lists each interview with its round, format, outcome, date, interviewer and notes. Last, it places the form answers component, which receives the application's saved answers and a save function.
sections.why: Likely reason: interviews and form answers are kept on the same record so the whole application stays in one place.
sections.watch_out: The save call is handed to the form answers component, so when a save happens is decided there and not in this section.

sections.name: window load handler (part 15)
sections.title: Timeline and metadata summary
sections.what: Builds a timeline that starts with when the job was sourced, then adds one line per interview, then a status line when the status is not sourced. The right column starts with a metadata box listing status, bucket, seniority, sector, remote, capture date and days in pipeline. Blank values show a dash.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a quick history of the application without the user digging through the record.
sections.watch_out: Dates are cut at the first T in the stored timestamp, so the display depends on that stored format staying the same.

sections.name: window load handler (part 16)
sections.title: Contacts list and source link
sections.what: Shows saved contacts in the right column, or a note that none exist yet. Contacts stored as plain text show as written, and other contacts show as raw JSON. Also shows a link to the original posting and adds https when it is missing.
sections.why: Likely reason: older records may store contacts as text and newer ones as objects, so both are handled.
sections.watch_out: Contacts saved as objects show as raw JSON text, which can look broken to the user.

sections.name: ApplicationPage
sections.title: Page wrapper with header and footer
sections.what: The outer shell of the application page. It places the header at the top, a loading message while the detail view loads, the detail view itself, and the footer.
sections.why: Likely reason: the detail view reads data from the page address, which Next.js requires to be wrapped in Suspense.
sections.watch_out: If the detail view never finishes loading, the user sees the LOADING message indefinitely.

summary: The main application detail screen: it shows one application, lets the user change its status and notes, generates documents with AI, exports them as printable pages, and logs updates in plain language.
purpose: Gives one place to work on a single job application from start to finish.
why: Likely reason: keeping all work on one screen saves the user from switching pages. The code does not state this.
how: Loads the application by slug from the web address and browser storage. Shows the title, status buttons, a box for plain-language updates, and the generation tools. Generation calls the AI helpers and saves results, and keeps a version history for undo. Status and notes save right away. The update box sends text to a parsing route and shows a preview before anything is saved. PDF export opens a print page in a new window.
inputs: The slug from the web address, the saved application, the candidate profile, model and integration settings, and the user's typing and clicks.
outputs: Updated application records, AI-generated documents, reminders, and a print window for PDF export.
risks: Many actions write to the same stored record, so an ordering mistake could drop a change. The PDF export places link addresses into HTML with limited escaping. The archive action permanently deletes. Only 11 of the 24 sections were reviewed, so parts of this file are unverified.
debug: If an application will not open, compare the slug in the address with stored applications. If generation fails, read the error under the action and check model settings. If an export is blank or missing, check that the popup was not blocked. If a status change does not stick, check the applications key in browser storage.
